findings.reason: implemented literally the instruction is either absent for every run or emitted on the flight key, so unfenced, resumed and operator-settings runs would be told to prefer a tool their launch never registered, and §8 would then report a share of anchored edits for an arm that had none.
findings.text: §5 says compose_prompt "adds, only for a run whose launch recorded anchored_edit: true, one instruction", but dispatch.py:2942 composes the prompt before the launch plan is built, and the anchored_edit fact is derived from that plan and written at dispatch.py:3372 (the `fenced` read it sits beside); compose_prompt takes no flag, no record and not even the backend mapping, so the stated condition cannot be evaluated where the section puts it, and the only value reachable at that point is the flight key — which §4 and §8 both say is not the arm split

findings.reason: a §5 node dispatched before §9 lands produces evidence that cannot be promoted, and the plan should either declare §5 depends-on §9 or keep the parser test reading docs/research/fixtures/codex-anchored-edit-stream.jsonl as the omp node did.
findings.text: §5's done-when copies the codex stream "into the test fixtures", i.e. under tests/, which is exactly the case §9 says "cannot be promoted, whichever way its arms are run": is_test_path (reckon/crew/node.py:1018) returns true for any path under a tests directory, so _node_test_files (reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:526) passes the .jsonl to pytest, which exits 4 and the arm reader records collected_no_test (promotion_records.py:623-638); §5 declares depends-on §3 only, so nothing orders it after §9

findings.reason: an implementer taking the option the section calls simpler lands a narrowing that keeps the same unpromotable outcome for any node writing a non-test .py under tests/, while the gate reports success, so the section's purpose is only met by the first rule and the done-when must test that distinction (a helper module under tests/ yields a command naming no test file).
findings.text: §9 offers two narrowing rules ("Python files matching the test-file pattern, or more simply the .py files is_test_path admits") but its done-when tests only a .jsonl fixture and a test_x.py, both of which the simpler rule passes; that rule still admits tests/conftest.py and tests/helpers.py, which pytest exits 5 on, and promotion_records.py:623 counts exits 4 and 5 alike as collected_no_test
